title: A Veil for the Sigil
premise: Isandro Voss, a cartographer of realms he has never visited, lives in a valley where magic cannot follow — the one place the old covenant between worlds cannot reach. When his name and tonight's date surface in a century-old book of prophecies, he is pulled through the veil into a realm unraveling at its seams. Guided by a disgraced sigil-keeper named Wren and her ragtag found family of exiles, Isandro discovers he is heir to the covenant's broken bloodline: the valley was never his refuge but his inheritance, forged by an ancestor who fled rather than reforge what was shattered. To save both realms, Isandro must return to the valley that raised him and remake the covenant with his own blood — knowing it may cost him the only home he has ever known. In the end, he learns belonging is not a place you inherit but a family you choose, and the reforged covenant binds not by blood alone but by those willing to stand on either side of the veil.
about_author: Rafael Iversen is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing maps of places that no longer exist. They write fantasy about people who find homes in the spaces between worlds.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. He finishes a map of a realm he has never seen, guided only by dreams, while the valley hums with its familiar magic-dead silence. A festival marks the centenary of the valley's founding. Emotional beat: quiet restlessness — Isandro loves his home yet feels like a guest in it.

chapters.title: Ink That Wasn't There Yesterday
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. At the archive, he finds a prophecy book dated a century past; fresh ink names him and tonight's date. The librarian warns him to burn it. He doesn't. Emotional beat: dread curdling into fascination as the impossible becomes personal.

chapters.title: What the Veil Took
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. At midnight, the prophecy fulfills itself: the veil tears open and drags him through. He lands in the realm of Veylmoor, where the sky is cracked and magic leaks like light from a wound. Emotional beat: terror and vertigo, the mapmaker finally inside the map.

chapters.title: A Keeper With Nothing Left to Keep
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren, last of the sigil-keepers, finds the stranger the prophecy promised and nearly leaves him for the hollowed ones. His blood reacts to her dying sigil instead. Emotional beat: wary hope in someone who has stopped hoping.

chapters.title: The Company of the Unwanted
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Isandro meets Wren's found family: Bramble, a hedge-witch exile; Ossian, a knight who broke his oaths; and Pip, a child who slipped through the veil years ago. Emotional beat: Isandro's first taste of warmth in a broken world.

chapters.title: The Covenant's Broken Spine
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Wren explains the covenant: five anchor-sigils binding the realms, four darkened, one failing. The valley is the fifth — hidden, magic-proof, built by a founder named Voss. Emotional beat: the sickening realization that his home is a wound in the world.

chapters.title: Road Through the Hollow Country
chapters.summary: Ossian's POV. The company travels toward the first anchor. Hollowed ones — people emptied by the covenant's decay — stalk them. Ossian recognizes one as his former commander. Emotional beat: grief for what the breaking costs, and resolve hardened by it.

chapters.title: The First Anchor Sings
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. At the drowned cathedral anchor, Isandro's blood briefly relights the sigil — proof of his inheritance, and proof the enemy will come for him. Emotional beat: awe shadowed by fear; he is useful, and therefore hunted.

chapters.title: The Regent's Summons
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Lady Sereth, regent of Veylmoor, offers sanctuary and an army to help Isandro reforge the covenant — if he does it under her control. Wren distrusts her instantly. Emotional beat: temptation versus instinct; the trap wears a kind face.

chapters.title: Pip's Map Home
chapters.summary: Pip's POV. Pip shows Isandro her own crayon map of the valley she barely remembers. He realizes the children taken through the veil were meant to be covenant-bearers too — and failed. Emotional beat: tenderness and guilt; Isandro sees what failure would mean.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Second Anchor
chapters.summary: Ossian's POV. At the mountain anchor, Sereth's soldiers arrive 'to help' — and seize the sigil-stone. Ossian learns Sereth plans to bind the covenant to herself alone. Emotional beat: bitter recognition; Ossian has been betrayed by oaths before.

chapters.title: Flight Into the Underveil
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Hunted, the company flees beneath the world into the Underveil, where the covenant's original architects left their records. Emotional beat: claustrophobic desperation giving way to wonder at the founders' true intentions.

chapters.title: The Founder's Confession
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. In the archives, Isandro reads his ancestor's confession: Aldous Voss didn't flee the covenant's collapse — he caused it, severing the fifth anchor to hoard safety for himself and his heirs. Emotional beat: shame and fury at an inheritance written in cowardice.

chapters.title: Wren's Broken Sigil
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren confesses why she was disgraced: she tried to reforge the covenant alone years ago and it killed her order, leaving her sigil scarred. She believes she is the reason Isandro must die to fix her mistake. Emotional beat: self-loathing met by Isandro's stubborn forgiveness — the found family deepens.

chapters.title: Sereth's Bargain
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Captured by Sereth, Isandro is offered a choice: reforge the covenant with her holding the anchors, saving Veylmoor but sealing the valley and everyone in it forever. Emotional beat: the seduction of a clean solution that requires sacrificing home.

chapters.title: The Third Anchor Burns
chapters.summary: Bramble's POV. Sereth forces a partial reforging; the third anchor ignites and the backlash hollows a whole town. Bramble saves whom she can. Emotional beat: horror and anger — half-measures have a body count, and time has officially run out.

chapters.title: What We Choose to Carry
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Escaping with Wren, Ossian, Bramble, and Pip, Isandro rejects both Sereth's control and his ancestor's cowardice. The reforging needs all five anchors held willingly — including the valley's. Emotional beat: quiet resolve; the plan is almost certainly fatal, and they commit anyway.

chapters.title: Storming the Spire
chapters.summary: Ossian's POV. The company assaults Sereth's spire where three stolen anchor-stones are held. Ossian duels his hollowed commander to free the stones. Emotional beat: catharsis — old debts paid, old wounds answered.

chapters.title: The Fourth Anchor and the Price of Names
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren channels her scarred sigil to hold the fourth anchor, burning out what remains of her keeper's gift. Isandro holds her as the light goes through them both. Emotional beat: sacrifice freely given; love stated plainly at the edge of ruin.

chapters.title: Through the Veil, Home
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Isandro crosses back into the valley — the first to do so in a century — and faces the fifth anchor in the heart of his hometown, as Sereth's forces and the collapsing veil converge. Emotional beat: homecoming turned battlefield; everything he loves in one fragile place.

chapters.title: A Veil Reforged
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Climax. Rather than seal the valley or sacrifice himself alone, Isandro calls the company through the veil — blood, oath, and choice together — and reforges the covenant so magic flows gently between realms instead of tearing them. Sereth falls trying to seize the power for herself. Emotional beat: triumph earned collectively, not inherited.

chapters.title: Cartographer of Both Worlds
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Months later, the valley opens its roads; Pip reunites with kin; Wren teaches new keepers. Isandro publishes a map of two realms joined at last, then goes home to a house full of the family he chose. Emotional beat: belonging fulfilled — inheritance transformed into invitation.
